import html # Pre‑defined HTML template with placeholders for the invitation fields. INVITATION_FORMAT = """ {event_title}
{event_title}
Date: {event_date}
{event_description}
{additional_notes}
""" def build_event_invitation( title_of_event: str, details_of_event: str, when_event_is: str, extra_event_info: str ) -> str: """ Build a secure HTML invitation for an event. All user supplied text is escaped to prevent XSS and other injection attacks. The resulting HTML uses a fixed template, ensuring that only the intended placeholders are replaced and no arbitrary tags can be injected. Args: title_of_event: The event's name or heading. details_of_event: A detailed description (may contain line breaks). when_event_is: The scheduled date of the event. extra_event_info: Any additional notes or instructions. Returns: A sanitized HTML string ready for rendering. """ # Escape all user input to neutralize malicious content safe_title = html.escape(title_of_event, quote=True) safe_description = html.escape(details_of_event, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") safe_date = html.escape(when_event_is, quote=True) safe_notes = html.escape(extra_event_info, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") # Format the invitation with the sanitized values invitation_html = INVITATION_FORMAT.format( event_title=safe_title, event_description=safe_description, event_date=safe_date, additional_notes=safe_notes ) return invitation_html
